title: Can you write 5,070 in two other ways?
description: Farhan counts the books in the school library. The video writes five thousand and seventy in expanded form and as Hundreds plus Ones.
teaching_notes: One idea: expanded form adds the digit values, and Hundreds plus Ones takes the Hundreds away and keeps the rest as Ones. Watch for a digit being read as Ones when it is in the tens place.

source: Your turn: write 5,070 in expanded form and as 50 Hundreds +
video_script.why: The child has met expanded form and Hundreds plus Ones and now tries both on one number with zeros in it.
video_script.substitution: Write the value of each digit and leave out zeros, then take the Hundreds away and count the rest as Ones.
video_script.anchor: Farhan counting the books in the school library
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says seven Ones because the digit is seven. The seven is in the tens place, so it is worth seventy.
video_script.payoff_line: a zero adds nothing, so we leave it out

final_answer.spoken: five thousand plus seventy, and fifty Hundreds plus seventy Ones

maths_rules: your turn: 3,090 = 3,000 + 90 and 30 Hundreds + 90 Ones; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: two ways to split a number, by digit values and by Hundreds plus Ones. Wrong idea: a tens digit read as Ones. The shelf and place boxes stay on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='lib'/>Farhan counts five thousand and seventy books in the school library.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write this number in expanded form. Expanded form means adding up the value of each digit. Then write it as fifty Hundreds plus some Ones.

narration: <bookmark mark='pv'/>The five is in the thousands place, so it is worth five thousand.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The zero in the hundreds place is worth nothing.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>The seven is in the tens place, so it is worth seventy. The last zero is in the ones place and is worth nothing.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Seven Ones, because the last digit that is not zero is seven.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>The seven is in the tens place, so it is worth seventy.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Fifty Hundreds plus seven Ones is only five thousand and seven.

beats.on_screen: the values 5,000, 0, 70 and 0 in a row with plus signs; the zeros fade out; the answer 5,000 + 70 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Add the value of each digit. Write five thousand plus zero plus seventy plus zero.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>A zero adds nothing, so we leave it out.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The expanded form is five thousand plus seventy.

beats.on_screen: 50 Hundreds shown as 5,000; 5,070 − 5,000 is written; the answer 50 Hundreds + 70 Ones is written

marks.ans: the answer 50 Hundreds + 70 Ones is written

narration: <bookmark mark='hun'/>Fifty Hundreds make five thousand, because each Hundred is worth one hundred.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Take five thousand away from five thousand and seventy.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Seventy is left, so five thousand and seventy is fifty Hundreds plus seventy Ones.
